p:cNvPr.descr: PART !: An illustration depicting the chemical logic of the glycolytic pathway. At the top is glucose on a line. It begins on the left with it bonding up to O, up to OH, down to OH, up to OH, up to OH and up to OH (in a pink box). Above this line are the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, all in pink. The numbers are placed above each step in the glucose line. To the right of glucose is a purple box that states, Phosphorylation of glucose ensures that pathway intermediates remain in the cell.” Below glucose is an arrow pointing down to the glucose 6-phosphate. To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from ATP to ADP (all in red). This is step 1: Phosphorylation occurs on C-6, as C-1 is a carbonyl group and cannot be phosphorylated. The glucose 6-phosphate line is the same as the glucose line but the first O is in a pink box, and the last point is O, which bonds right to P in a circle, all in a pink box. This has an arrow pointing from the first O in glucose 6-phosphate down and right to O in a pink box on the fructose 6-phosphate line. This is step 2: Isomerization moves the carbonyl to C-2, a prerequisite for steps 3 and 4. The fructose 6-phosphate line begins with it bonding up to HO, up to O (in a pink box), down to OH, up to OH, up to OH, and up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. This has an arrow below pointing from O in the pink box of fructose 6-phosphate to the first point of the line for fructose 1,6-bisphosphate. To the left of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from ATP to ADP (all in red). This is step 3: C-1, now bearing a hydroxyl group, can be phosphorylated. This ensures that both products of C—C bond cleavage are phosphorylated, and thus interconvertible. The fructose 1.6-biphosphate line is the same as fructose 6-phosphate, but the first point bonds up to O, which bonds left to P in a circle, all in a pink box. The second O is not in a pink box, and there is a wavy red line that crosses the line between the third and fourth points. The second O in this line has an arrow pointing down to dihydroxyacetone phosphate line, which begins bonding up to O, which bonds left to P in a circle. The second point double bonds up to O and the last point bonds up to OH. The last two points are all in a pink box. The OH point in the fructose 1.6-bisphosphate has an arrow pointing down to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. This is step 4: The carbonyl group at C-2 facilitates C—C bond cleavage at the right location to yield two 3-carbon products by the reverse of an aldol condensation.

p:cNvPr.descr: PART 2: An illustration depicting the chemical logic of the glycolytic pathway. Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate’s line begins double bonding up to O, the second point bonding up to OH, and the last point bonding up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. The first two points are in a pink box. This line has reversible arrows pointing from the pink box to the pink box up and left to the pink box in dihydroxyacetone phosphate. This is step 5: Interconversion of the two products of step 4 funnels both products into a single pathway. Below the pink box in glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate points down to the pink box in 1.3-bisphosphoglycerate. To the right of this arrow is a curved arrow pointing from NAD+, Pi to NADH all in red. This is step 6: Oxidative phosphorylation of glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, with on NADH produced, is a prerequisite for ATP production in step 7. The 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate begins by double bonding up to O and down and left to P in a circle, which bonds right to O (in a pink box). The second point bonds up to OH, and the third point bonds up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. Below this is an arrow pointing from the pink box in 1.3-bisphosphoglycerate to the first pink box in 3-phosphoglycerate. To the left of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from ADP to ATP all in red. This is step 7: ATP production. The 3-phosphoglycerate line begins double bonding up to O and bonding down to –O. –O is in a pink box. The second point bonds up to OH, and the third line bonds up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. The last point is in a pink box. Below this is an arrow pointing from the second pink box in 3-phosphoglycerate to the pink box of 2-phosphoglycerate. This is step 8: The remaining phosphoryl group moves from C-2 to C-3, setting up the final steps of the pathway. The 2-phosphoglycerate line begins by double bonding up to O, and bonded down and left to –O. The second point bonds up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle (on a pink box). The third point bonds down to OH. This pink box has an arrow pointing down to the pink box in phosphoenolpyruvate. This is step 9: Dehydration activates the phosphoryl for transfer to ADP in step 10. The phosphoenolpyruvate line begins double bonding up to O and bonds down and left to –O. The second point bonds up to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. There is also a double bond on the line to the right. The second point is in a pink box. An arrow points from this pink box down to the pink box in pyruvate. To the right is a curved arrow from ADP to ATP (all in red). This is step 10: ATP production. The pyruvate line begins double bonding up to O and bonds down and left to –O. The second point double bonds up to O (in a pink box).
